Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with `README.md`, then I’ll follow the named `fish-control-primitives` skill and the wake-visual inspection skill before touching the policy. I’ll keep the implementation to one candidate and won’t run CFD unless the workspace explicitly directs it.

The workspace requires the assigned guidance, four sampled solver evaluations, and a pre-edit visual diagnosis. I’m reading the two skill contracts now; their immediate effect is that I’ll separate transferable control invariants from source-specific kinematics and inspect both prescribed wake views before proposing the architecture.

The inherited guidance says the current decision boundary is narrow: preserve the successful carrier and course bend, avoid another counter-tangent, and test hydrodynamic response as a smooth admission gate for posterior amplitude relief. I’ll now verify that against every sampled rollout and the inherited optimizer notes, including initialization, trajectory, loads, and actuator exposure—not just the nearly tied scores.

All four are valid direct-uniform still-water captures, so there is no terminal failure in this sample; the informative contrast is the best-score counter-tangent case (`28b…`) versus the cleaner response-relief variants with nearly identical capture progress. I’m inspecting all four combined top-down/oblique sheets so any claimed wake difference is visually grounded.

The visual sheets are effectively topology-identical: each fish self-propels along the same broad curved approach, building a coherent alternating mid-plane street and compact three-dimensional Lambda2 structures through capture. That makes the trace data decisive. The assigned parent’s own post-exit rollout is also available in inherited logs, so I’m including it—especially because its load-gated relief was unevaluated when the parent wrote its hypothesis.

The assigned parent’s result falsifies its intended benefit: moment-gating leaves arrival unchanged from unconditional relief (`23.8755T`) while worsening inside-`3L` yaw (`1.634` vs `1.606 rad/T`), lateral force (`0.00904` vs `0.00889`), and yaw moment (`0.00622` vs `0.00614`). I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a replacement invariant; this skill action will inform only a normalized body-frame, two-joint mechanism, not imported gains or phase schedules.

The selected architecture is one compact mechanism: keep the evidenced C-bend carrier and posterior half-cycle relief, but replace instantaneous load gating with smooth target-course urgency. Carrier-rejected yaw chooses the dissipative direction, joint state chooses the affected stroke, and normalized target-relative cross-track residual redistributes relief strength without changing its sampled average. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification boundary before editing, as required by the visual skill.

The notes are now in place before the edit. I’m implementing the single candidate by replacing the prefilled counter-tangent/load gate with course-urgent posterior wave relief; the carrier, course bend, redirect release, and smooth command projection remain unchanged.

The candidate now uses course residual only as a smooth magnitude cue; it does not choose turn sign or phase. I’m materializing the durable lesson from the parent’s failed moment gate in `control_experience.md`, explicitly warning later workers that instantaneous reactive load is not yet a validated relief trigger.

The reusable guidance now records the parent’s concrete negative result and its future boundary. Before invoking the required check-runner, I’m running the same lightweight guidance and boundary checks locally so I can repair any issue immediately; no CFD will be started.

The local checks pass: guidance is materially changed, the solver boundary is clean, the candidate is non-empty with one public policy/parameter definition, and all 69 direct `params.FIELD` references are declared. Julia is not installed in this workspace, so I’m now invoking the required check-runner agent; it will independently run the configured non-CFD checks and report the runtime limitation if it persists.

The configured check-runner invocation was attempted, but its fixed `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account, so the agent could not start. I’m completing the exact configured checks directly: guidance and boundary already pass; the only unavailable check is Julia execution, which I’m covering with deterministic schema/structure checks and a close diff against the evaluated amplitude-relief policy.

The close diff confirms the policy change is limited to course-urgency allocation layered onto the evaluated relief controller; no forbidden time, route, cylinder, random, or mutable state entered the policy. Because the dedicated runner’s fixed model could not launch, I’m using a supported read-only checker as a fallback to execute and audit the same `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml` contract independently.

The fallback audit is still running. The current workspace state already satisfies the two executable checks and the deterministic schema guard; I’m doing one final materiality/file-scope pass while it finishes.

All direct final checks now pass: material guidance update, solver boundary, one non-empty candidate, complete parameter schema, required bookshelf provenance, and clean whitespace. The independent fallback checker appears delayed, so I’m asking it for its current result rather than letting validation stall.

The fallback checker agrees: guidance and boundary pass; static schema, state fields, call arities, delimiters, and the two-element `phi_ddot` contract all pass. The Julia execution remains indeterminate only because `julia` is not installed—not because of a policy failure—and no CFD was run.

Produced exactly one candidate: `dogfish_3d_target_v32_course_urgent_posterior_amplitude_relief`.

- [Visual diagnosis, hypothesis, and bookshelf transfer](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable negative lesson from the failed moment gate](guidance/control_experience.md:65)

Guidance, boundary, parameter-schema, arity, delimiter, and static contract checks pass. The configured check-runner was invoked but its fixed model was unsupported; a fallback checker independently confirmed the results. Julia execution was unavailable because `julia` is not installed. No CFD was run.
